faq.a: Siddiq is associated with the Arabic form صِدِّيق, whose core sense is siddiq; truthful, sincere.

faq.q: What is the origin of Siddiq?
faq.a: Siddiq is associated with Arabic. Siddiq is Arabic صِدِّيق (Ṣiddīq), an intensive form meaning 'truthful, sincere'.
Yes — the underlying form صِدِّيق is Arabic.
Siddiq can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Siddiq should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ص د ق is Quranic, but Ṣiddīq is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Siddiq mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Siddiq is rendered صدیق and carries the sense صدیق، سچا.

faq.q: What does Siddiq mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Siddiq is rendered صدیق and carries the sense صدیق، راستگو.
A romanized syllable approximation is sid-diq. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Siddiq?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Siddiq, siddiq. Script forms are صديق, صدیق, صِدِّيق, सिद्दीक़.

faq.q: Is Siddiq a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
